title: Tiramisu
subtitle: Italian espresso and mascarpone dessert
excerpt: The great Italian dessert: savoiardi biscuits soaked in strong espresso and Marsala, layered with a rich, airy cream of mascarpone, egg yolks, and sugar, and dusted with bitter cocoa. Made a day ahead; it only improves with time.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tiramisu (pick me up or lift me up) is a dessert first documented in the Veneto region of Italy in the early 1970s, with the Le Beccherie restaurant in Treviso often credited as its origin, though this is disputed by others. The dessert has become one of the most widely eaten Italian dishes in the world. The classic version uses raw egg yolks whisked with sugar to form a zabaglione-like cream with mascarpone, layered with savoiardi (ladyfinger biscuits) soaked in strong espresso and a small amount of Marsala or rum. Modern versions that pasteurise the eggs by making the zabaglione over a water bath are safer and produce a stable cream; the traditional version uses raw yolks. The version here uses the safer cooked method.

content.text: The mascarpone cream must be thick enough to hold its shape in layers; if it is too soft, fold it gently to avoid deflating the egg yolks. Dip the biscuits quickly in the coffee and do not soak them: a momentary dip on each side is enough. Over-soaked biscuits collapse into a soggy mess. The tiramisu must rest in the fridge for at least 4 hours; overnight is better.

Whisk the egg yolks and sugar in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of gently simmering water (the bowl must not touch the water). Whisk for 5 to 8 minutes until the mixture is very thick, pale, and has tripled in volume. Remove from the heat and leave to cool for 10 minutes.
Fold the mascarpone into the cooled egg mixture in two additions until smooth. Fold in the whipped cream gently. Mix the cooled espresso with the Marsala in a wide, shallow bowl.

Quickly dip each biscuit in the coffee for 1 second per side and lay in a single layer in a large dish. Spread half the mascarpone cream over. Repeat with the remaining biscuits and cream. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours. Dust generously with cocoa powder immediately before serving.
